comparator.name: International Bachelor History
comparator.route: Social History focus area with minor/internship option
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme is a three-year, 180-EC history bachelor. Year 1 is common; from year 2 students choose Economic History, International Relations, Social History or Cultural History. The neutral Social History focus area is used because it retains the broadest historical-social identity without choosing a UCR-favourable specialist route. The third year includes profile space and culminates in public-history work, a thesis class and a bachelor thesis.
components: Global and modern history survey courses
Historical sources, historiography and first-year writing
Neutral focus-area selection used for the generic History target.
Quantitative and qualitative historical methods plus electives
Minor, internship or elective profile space

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Global, early-modern and modern historical development
Historical interpretation, periodisation and connections between past and present
Primary sources, historical methods, research design and scholarly writing
Social change, migration, inequality and changing communities
Culture, identity, heritage and public memory
Academic communication and the public role of historical knowledge
questions: How do global connections, institutions and power shape societies over time?
How can historical sources and methods clarify present-day public problems?

selection.assessment: The broad closest match captures historical development, source criticism, social history, culture and public communication. Economic History and International Relations each provide a coherent, feasible and substantially distinct additional direction. Cultural History is already represented inside the closest-match curriculum. History education is not included as a separate pathway because UCR does not provide the pedagogy, supervised school practice or teaching qualification needed for a defensible education route. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

alternatives.label: Global, social & cultural history
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines global and modern history with sociology, heritage, art, literature, media and historical research; the label states that interdisciplinary centre without claiming a complete specialist History major.
alternatives.concept: A broad history pathway linking global and modern historical change to social relations, culture, heritage, public memory and research practice.
progression: Introductory historical, sociological, cultural and communication courses precede advanced seminars. The History Research Seminar is placed in year 3 after substantial history and qualitative-methods preparation. Every formal prerequisite is earlier and all courses are assigned to offered semesters.

alternatives.label: Economic history, institutions & inequality
alternatives.labelReason: History and social theory are combined with economics, statistics and quantitative methods to make long-run economic change and inequality the explicit organising direction.
alternatives.concept: An Economic History direction connecting historical change and institutions with economics, inequality, quantitative evidence and public policy.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the closest match’s art, heritage, literature and media content with economics, statistics, data science and mathematics, shifting the centre to long-run economic development and inequality.
progression: Economics, business and data foundations precede public economics, econometrics and behavioural economics. Historical methods and surveys precede the final research seminar. All courses are offered in their assigned semesters.

alternatives.label: History, international relations & global power
alternatives.labelReason: The course set joins modern and global history to international relations, conflict, comparative politics and public international law, making global power the visible organising strand.
alternatives.concept: An International Relations direction using historical development to examine diplomacy, conflict, law, institutions and changing global power.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most economics and cultural-heritage courses with international relations, peace and conflict, comparative politics and international law, creating a clearly different global-power curriculum.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes the level-200 and level-300 law courses. Introductory political and historical courses precede advanced international-relations and conflict study; the History Research Seminar remains in year 3. All courses are offered in their assigned semesters.

notes.text: UCR can construct a strong interdisciplinary historical pathway but cannot reproduce the comparator’s full continuous specialist History sequence, archival training, focus-area menu, school-teaching qualification or dedicated supervised history thesis.

routeSelection.route: Social History focus area with minor/internship option
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic History. The official curriculum requires a focus area from year 2. Social History is selected because it preserves the programme’s broad historical-social identity and is not chosen for ease of matching to UCR.
